about: AMPLE beats catalogue. Original, CC0 patterns in the style of widely known groove families (no recording is copied). Every grid is 16 steps per bar: x hit, X accent, o ghost, . rest. Voice names (kick, snare, hat, openhat, clap, rim, ride, tom, shaker, cowbell) follow the common kit names; a kit may use others (map them). novelty: 1 = everywhere, safe as a background; 5 = rare and distinctive, use sparingly. energy and density: 1 calm/sparse .. 5 intense/busy. Ids are stable.

house.why: short offbeat stabs leave room for the kick
offbeat or rolling bass between the kicks
slow chords that open over 8 bars

hiphop.why: a looped 2-bar sample-like phrase carries the track

lofi.why: mellow extended chords are the identity of the style

kinds: soft finger bass or round sub
lofi.why: walks little, stays on roots and fifths
gentle arpeggio on top of the chords
tiny melodic notes now and then

trap.why: the 808 is the bass line and the kick partner
sparse minor melody over the heavy low end
ear-catching hook with space around it

rock.why: chords on the beat carry the groove
eighth notes on the root lock to the kick
melody or riff in the verse gaps
fills the chords without crowding the guitar

funk.why: syncopated, leaves a rest on the one's neighbour

kinds: clean short chop on beats 2 and 4 (the skank)
reggae.why: the offbeat chop is the style
the bass carries the melody; keep it simple and slow

dnb.why: slow half-time bass line against the fast drums
liquid style leans on lush chords

latin.why: the piano figure locks to the clave
the bossa and samba comping instrument

afro.why: two interlocking patterns make the groove
a repeating riff, not a chord-root line

jazz.why: four notes per bar, steps and chord tones

kinds: clean or slightly crunchy shuffle chords
upright or finger bass, boogie pattern

blues.why: call and response with the vocal

ambient.why: the bed everything else sits on

kinds: short acid lead or square pluck

country.why: fills at the end of phrases

ballad.why: the arpeggio keeps time at slow tempo

kinds: soft finger bass or sustained sub

beats.name: House: four on the floor
beats.say: BOOM . clap . | BOOM . clap . | with a 'tss' hat on every 'and'
tips: Keep the kick on every beat all the way; vary the other parts, not the kick.
Open the hat only on the offbeats; a closed hat on the beats muddies the kick.
Drop the kick for 1 or 2 bars before the chorus for a break, then bring it back on the downbeat.
howToBringIn: Start with kick + hat for 8 bars, add the clap at bar 9, then bass, then chords.
A 4-bar build: add snare roll (every 8th, then every 16th) and remove it on the next downbeat.
beats.fast: Above 130 it turns towards techno or hard dance; keep the pattern, the hats can become 16ths.
beats.slow: Below 118 it feels like deep house/downtempo; swing the hats a little (0.1-0.2).

drums.fill: snare:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx on the last bar before a section

bass.text: offbeat 'and' notes on the root (a 'pum-pa'), or rolling 8ths

chords.rhythm: short stab on the 'and' of 2 and 4

avoid: busy hi-hat rolls on top of the offbeat hat

beats.name: Boom bap
beats.say: BOOM . . . | CLAP . . BOOM | . BOOM . . | CLAP . . .
tips: Snare on 2 and 4 hard, kicks around beat 1 and the 'and' of 3.
Swing the 16ths about 0.15-0.25; a little late snare feels human.
A short ghost snare before beat 4 makes it roll.
howToBringIn: Let the sample loop (2 bars) play 2 bars alone, then enter the drums.
Cut the drums for the last beat of a 4-bar phrase and let a vocal line land there.
beats.fast: Above ~100 it starts to feel like a jog; switch to the half-time trap feel instead.
beats.slow: Below 80 the hats need to move on 16ths to keep time.

bass.text: root on the kick hits, a pickup note before the loop restarts

chords.progression: i - iv - V (or a 2-bar minor 7th sample loop)
chords.rhythm: one chord per bar, slightly behind the beat

beats.name: Lo-fi chill
beats.say: boom . . . | tk . . boom | . . boom . | tk . . .  (soft, behind the beat)
tips: Soft velocities (60-90), hats quiet; leave the beat a bit loose with humanize 0.3-0.5.
Swing 0.25-0.35 is the lo-fi shuffle.
Add vinyl-like noise and a gentle low-pass for the 'old tape' feel.
howToBringIn: Start with the chords alone for 2 bars, drums enter at bar 3.
Keep sections identical for long stretches; change only a layer every 8 bars.
beats.fast: Above ~90 it loses the sleepy feel; use boom bap.
beats.slow: Below 70 it works as a dreamy ballad bed.

bass.text: long soft root notes, sometimes a fifth

chords.progression: ii7 - V7 - Imaj7 - vi7 (or Imaj7 - iii7 - vi7 - IV)

beats.name: Trap half-time
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . BOOM . | SNARE . . . | . BOOM . .  with fast 'ti-ti-ti-ti' hat rolls
tips: Count it as 70 bpm: the snare lands on beat 3 of the bar (the middle) so it feels half-time.
Hats are 8ths with triplet or 32nd rolls once per 2 bars; vary velocities.
The 808 sits on the kick; let it ring then cut it before the next hit.
howToBringIn: Intro with melody only, 808 drops on the hook.
Silence for one beat before the drop makes it hit harder.
beats.fast: Above 150 the hat rolls get too busy; use fewer.
beats.slow: Below 130 use the plain boom bap.

bass.text: 808 on every kick hit, glide between notes, long tail

chords.rhythm: sparse notes, a lot of space

beats.name: Rock: straight eighths
beats.say: BOOM tss SNARE tss | BOOM BOOM SNARE tss  (hat on every 8th)
tips: Snare on 2 and 4, the hat holds steady 8ths.
A kick on the 'and' of 3 adds drive.
Crash on beat 1 at the start of a chorus.
howToBringIn: Use hat or ride only for the verse, add open hat/crash at the chorus.
A 1-bar tom fill leads into a new section.
beats.fast: Above 140 it becomes punk; keep it simple and play 8ths on the hat.
beats.slow: Below 100 go to a ballad feel with a half-time snare.

chords.rhythm: strums on every beat or every 8th

avoid: soft electronic pads at the front

beats.name: Rock: driving punk 8ths
beats.say: BOOM-tss-SNARE-tss, snare every other beat; kick doubles up (boom boom)
tips: Hat/ride in constant 8ths, snare on 2 and 4 (or the d-beat variant on every 'and').
Keep the hits dry and loud; no ghost notes.
howToBringIn: Count in with 4 snare hits, then start.
Stop everything on a pause for a beat to make the return stronger.
beats.fast: At 190+ play half of the hat notes (quarters).
beats.slow: Below 150 it turns into regular rock.

beats.name: Disco
beats.say: BOOM TSS BOOM TSS: kick every beat, open 'tsss' hat on every 'and', snare/clap on 2 and 4
tips: 16th hat underneath with the open hat on the offbeats.
The bass plays octaves on the eighth notes.
howToBringIn: Strings sweep up for 2 bars into the chorus.
Bring the guitar in 8 bars after the drums.

bass.text: octave jumps on 8ths (root, octave, root, octave)

beats.name: Motorik
beats.say: BOOM-tss-BOOM-tss: kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4, hat on every 8th, never stopping
tips: The point is that nothing changes; keep fills very rare.
A constant, unaccented hat drives the loop.
howToBringIn: Start with the drums alone, then add a single repeating bass line.
Add layers every 16 bars.
beats.fast: Over 145 turns into a rush; fine for a driving chase.

beats.name: Reggae: one drop
beats.say: . . . . | . . . . | KICK+RIM . . . | . . . .  (nothing on beat 1; kick and snare land together on beat 3)
tips: Leave beat 1 empty: it is the 'drop'.
Chords chop on the 'and' of each beat (the skank); the bass plays long melodic notes.
howToBringIn: Let the bass carry the intro, add the skank at bar 3.
Use echo/delay on the snare in dub sections.
beats.fast: Above 90 it turns into ska (use the same offbeat chop).
beats.slow: Below 66 it feels like dub: remove the hats.

bass.text: melodic, long notes, lots of rests, root and minor 3rd/5th

chords.progression: I - IV - V - IV (or a one-chord vamp)
chords.rhythm: short chop on the 'and' of every beat

beats.name: Dub steppers
beats.say: BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM (every beat), rim on 3, long delay tails
tips: Kick on every beat gives a marching feel; the bass leaves wide gaps.
Automate delay sends on the snare/rim.
howToBringIn: Strip back to kick + bass in the break, bring the skank back with a delay throw.
Use few instruments.
beats.fast: Faster than 90 loses the heavy feel.
beats.slow: Below 70 gets very heavy: great for cinematic scenes.

beats.name: Drum and bass: two-step
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | . . BOOM . | SNARE . . .  (snare on 2 and 4 of a fast bar, kick on 1 and a late 3)
tips: Feel it as half time (86 bpm): kick on 1, snare on 3, bass slow and heavy.
Ghost snares between backbeats and hats on 8ths make it roll.
howToBringIn: Start with the pad and bass, the drums drop after 16 bars with a roll.
8-bar bass variation, 16-bar drop.
beats.fast: Above 178 it is rarely danceable; reduce hat density.
beats.slow: Below 160 sounds like a breakbeat track.

bass.text: slow, in half time: one note per beat, long and heavy

chords.progression: i - VI - iv - v (liquid) or one long chord

beats.name: Breakbeat (syncopated)
beats.say: BOOM . boom . | SNARE . ss SNARE | . boom . . | SNARE . . ss  (kicks and snares scattered, hat on all 16ths)
tips: Ghost snares (o) between the main hits give the chopped feel.
Vary velocity of the hats.
howToBringIn: Play it without bass for 4 bars, then drop a sub.
Chop to half-time for a break.
beats.slow: Below 100 sounds like a hip-hop break.

beats.name: Bossa nova
beats.say: BOOM . . boom | . . BOOM . | . . boom . | tk .  (a soft 'bom-ba-bom', cross-stick on the offbeats)
tips: Kick plays the bass-drum figure (1, 'and' of 2, 3, 'and' of 4), the rim plays the clave.
Keep dynamics very soft; the guitar and bass carry the groove.
howToBringIn: Start with nylon guitar alone for 2 bars.
Bass joins at bar 3, light drums at bar 5.

bass.text: root on 1 and the fifth on 'and' of 2, repeating

beats.name: Clave groove (son 3-2)
beats.say: click . . click | . . click . | . . . . | click . click .  (clave 3-2) with the kick on every beat
tips: Everything must agree with the clave; do not change the side halfway.
Shaker steady 16ths, cowbell on beats.
howToBringIn: Start with the clave and shaker only, bass enters, then piano montuno.
A 'cierre' (stop) on beat 1 of the new section.
beats.fast: Above 130 gets very fast and busy (timba).

chords.progression: i - iv - V7 - i (montuno repeats every 2 bars)
chords.rhythm: syncopated piano figure that agrees with the clave

beats.name: Afrobeat
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . boom . | SNARE . . boom | . . SNARE .  with a busy, syncopated hat
tips: Many layers play small interlocking patterns; keep each simple.
Grooves run 8-16 minutes in the original style: build slowly.
howToBringIn: Drums + bass first, one guitar after 8 bars, the second one after 16, horns last.
Never stop the groove completely.

chords.progression: one chord (a long vamp) or I - IV

beats.name: Blues shuffle
beats.say: BOOM-a tss-a SNARE-a tss-a: long-short, long-short (a 'dah-dih dah-dih' triplet feel)
tips: Set the swing to about 0.66 so 8ths become long-short.
A 12-bar form: 4 bars I, 2 bars IV, 2 bars I, V, IV, I, V (turnaround).
howToBringIn: Start with one guitar riff, drums enter on bar 2 with just hat.
The turnaround in the last 2 bars signals the next chorus.
beats.fast: Above 120 it becomes a jump blues/rockabilly.
beats.slow: Below 70 it is a slow blues: use 12/8 triplets.

bass.text: boogie pattern: root, root, fifth, sixth (shuffle)

chords.progression: I7 - IV7 - I7 - V7 (12 bar blues)

beats.name: Funk: 16th-note groove
beats.say: BOOM . . boom | SNARE . ss SNARE | . boom . . | SNARE . ss ss  (ghost 'ss' between the big hits)
tips: The 'one' is the strongest beat: land the kick and bass together on it.
Ghost snares at low velocity (30-45) keep the groove alive.
Leave rests: funk is made of the gaps.
howToBringIn: Drums and bass lock for 4 bars before anything else.
A stop on beat 1 then a hit on the 'one' is classic.

chords.progression: one chord (dominant 9th vamp) or i7 - IV7

beats.name: Ballad (half-time)
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | SNARE . . . | . . . .  (one low kick, one soft snare in the bar)
tips: Snare on 3 gives half-time; let the chords carry the time.
Add 8th-note hat or ride for movement in the chorus.
howToBringIn: Only piano in the first verse, drums enter in the second verse.
Build with strings in the last chorus.
beats.fast: Above 80 it is a mid-tempo pop song.
beats.slow: Below 55 the arpeggio must do the work.

beats.name: Techno
beats.say: BOOM . . . | BOOM . . . | BOOM . . . | BOOM . . .  with clap on 2 and 4 and a closed hat on every 'and'
tips: Filter sweeps and subtle changes every 8 bars are the arrangement.
A rumble tail on the kick (reverb, low-passed) gives a sense of space.
howToBringIn: Kick alone for 16 bars, hats, clap, then bass.
Remove the kick for 8 bars as a break.

beats.name: UK garage 2-step
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | . . BOOM . | SNARE . . .  with skippy, swung hats (a 'tsk-ka-tsk-ka')
tips: The missing kick on beat 3 (2-step) is the identity.
Swing 0.35-0.45; sprinkle shuffled hats.
howToBringIn: Vocal chop first, then the beat and a pitched sub.
Ghost kick and snare shuffles.
beats.fast: Above 140 sounds like a drum and bass-ish skippy track.

beats.name: Dembow (reggaeton)
beats.say: BOOM . . . | BOOM . ch . | . ch BOOM . | ch . ch .  → 'boom-ch-boom-chick' repeated
tips: Kick on every beat, a snare/rim on the 'and' of 1 and on 4 (the dembow).
Bass follows the kick but is short.
howToBringIn: Intro with the vocal hook, drop with the dembow on the chorus.
Reggaeton drum fills are short single hits.

bass.text: short boomy notes on the kicks

beats.name: Country: train beat
beats.say: BOOM chick BOOM chick: kick on 1 and 3, 'brush' snare on every 8th with accents on 2 and 4
tips: Snare plays steady 8ths at low velocity with the backbeat accented.
Bass alternates root and fifth.
howToBringIn: Acoustic guitar alone for 2 bars, then brushes.
Fiddle fills at the end of phrases.
beats.fast: Above 160 is bluegrass: remove the drums.

bass.text: root-fifth alternation on the quarter notes

beats.name: Jazz swing (ride)
beats.say: ding . ding-a | ding . ding-a:  'spang-a-lang' on the ride, hat 'chick' on 2 and 4, kick feathered very softly
tips: Swing set to about 0.66; the ride plays beat 1, 2, 'and' of 2, 3, 4, 'and' of 4.
Kick is feathered very softly on every beat; snare comps sparsely.
howToBringIn: Bass walks alone for 4 bars; the ride enters.
Trade fours with a solo instrument.
beats.fast: Above ~180 leave out the kick and the hat; only ride + bass.
beats.slow: Below 100 becomes a ballad with brushes.

bass.text: walking: one note per beat, stepwise, ending on a chord tone

beats.name: Ambient heartbeat
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | . . boom . | . . . .  a slow soft heartbeat with one tiny shaker
tips: Use for underscore or a scene that must not draw attention.
Soft velocities, low-pass the kick.
howToBringIn: Fade in over 8 bars with a pad.
Drop out for long sections.

beats.name: Half-time heavy (dubstep style)
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | SNARE . . . | . . . .  (just kick on 1, snare on 3, all the weight in the bass)
tips: The sparse drums make space for the bass wobble.
Hats on 8ths, snare reverb.
howToBringIn: Long intro with a pad, drop with the bass on bar 1.
Silence before the drop.
beats.fast: Faster than 150 feels like drum and bass.
avoid: mid-range chords that fight the bass

beats.name: Slow shuffle in three (6/8 feel in 4/4 grid)
beats.say: BOOM-ta-ta SNARE-ta-ta: a rolling triplet 'one-and-a two-and-a'
tips: Use swing 0.66 to approximate the triplet grid in a 16-step bar; ideally use a 12-step triplet pattern if the kit allows it.
Great for old soul and doo-wop.
howToBringIn: Start with the piano triplets alone.
Add backing vocals in the second verse.
beats.slow: Below 50 gets too slow for the triplets.

beats.name: Heartbeat bed
beats.say: dum . . . | . dum . . | . . . . | . . . .  (two very soft kicks, like a pulse, nothing else)
tips: Keep the kick at about -12 dB so the voice stays in front.
No hats at all: the silence between the beats is the groove.
Let a pad or a long piano chord fill the space.
howToBringIn: Start with the pad alone, the heartbeat enters after four bars.
In the chorus add a soft brush hat, not more.
beats.fast: Above 70 it starts to feel like a march.
beats.slow: Below 48 the pulse is too far apart to hold the song together; let a bass note per bar help.

beats.name: Brush whisper
beats.say: shhh . shh-shh | shhh . shh-shh  (a soft brush swirl, a very quiet kick on 1)
tips: Use the hat as the brush, very low (-14 dB), with a gentle swing.
Rim on 2 and 4 is barely audible: a whisper, not a click.
Lead with a muted upright bass and a soft piano.
howToBringIn: Piano and voice first, the brushes join at the second verse.
Drop the kick in the bridge for extra air.
beats.fast: Above 76 it turns into a slow swing, add a ride.
beats.slow: Below 54 the brushes sound dragged; halve the hat to quarter notes.

beats.name: Slow sway (6/8 feel)
beats.say: BOOM . . dum . . | . . SNARE . . .  (a rocking 1-2-3 4-5-6, soft kick, soft snare)
tips: Think of two big beats, each with three small ones: feel the rock.
A triplet swing on the hat (s0.66) gives the sway.
Great under a long, sung line with few words.
howToBringIn: Start with the hat swing and an acoustic guitar or piano.
Kick and snare enter at the first chorus.
beats.fast: Above 66 it becomes a shuffle ballad.
beats.slow: Below 46 let the hat carry the triplets alone.

beats.name: No drums, only a pulse pad
beats.say: (no drums) | pad swells in, one soft shaker tick on each beat  (the voice is the rhythm)
tips: Use this when the singing must be the star: the pad and a quiet shaker or tick give the pulse.
Change the chord every two bars so it does not stand still.
Add a soft kick only for the last chorus.
howToBringIn: Pad and voice for the whole first verse.
Add the shaker tick in the second verse, a kick only in the last chorus.
beats.fast: Above 80 add a real hat so it does not drift.
beats.slow: Below 40 it needs a sung melody that moves.

beats.name: Lullaby waltz
beats.say: BOOM . . . | tick . tick . | (one big beat, two soft ones, in three)
tips: In 3/4 one bar is 12 steps: use a 12-step grid, it repeats on its own.
Keep the kick at the start of the bar only, very soft.
A music box or a soft piano plays the melody.
howToBringIn: Music box or piano alone for the first lines.
The soft kick enters at the second verse.
beats.fast: Above 74 it becomes a regular waltz.
beats.slow: Below 50 the three beats fall apart; play the chord on beat 1 only.

beats.name: Dusty swing hip hop
beats.say: BOOM . . boom | . . SNAP . | . boom . . | SNAP . . .  (the kick stumbles, the snare stays on 2 and 4)
tips: Swing the hats about 58 percent, the kick slightly late.
Let a dusty piano loop carry the harmony.
Cut the hat on the chorus to leave room for a rapper or singer.
howToBringIn: Loop first, then hat, then kick and snare on the second pass.
beats.fast: Above 94 it reads as a faster hip hop; keep the swing.

bass.text: short low notes after the kick

beats.name: Lo-fi rainy window
beats.say: boom . . . | . . snap . | . . boom . | . . snap .  (soft, a little behind, tape-like)
tips: Low-pass everything, add a gentle hiss.
Keep the snare quiet (about -10 dB), the hat is just a whisper.
Perfect as a bed under a quiet vocal.
howToBringIn: Chords alone for two bars, then the beat enters.
beats.fast: Above 80 it feels like a normal chill beat.
beats.slow: Below 62 turn it into the heartbeat bed.

beats.name: Trap rolling hats
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | SNAP . . boom | . . . . + hats rolling tt-tt-tt  (half-time, hats run in bursts)
tips: The snare stands on beat 3 of every bar; the hats roll in the last beat.
A long 808 bass note follows the kick.
Use the hat rolls at the end of a phrase only.
howToBringIn: Sub bass and snare first, the rolling hats from the second half of the verse.
beats.slow: Below 130 it becomes a heavy half-time beat.

beats.name: Slow funk pocket
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . SNAP . | . boom . boom | SNAP . . .  (space in the kick, ghost notes on the snare)
tips: Ghost snares (o) between the main hits give the pocket.
Keep the hats tight and quiet.
Bass and kick should lock; leave space for the voice.
howToBringIn: Bass and hat first, the snare enters at bar 5.
beats.fast: Above 98 it becomes a bright funk.

beats.name: Soft disco strut
beats.say: boom . . . | boom . . . | boom . . . | boom . . .  with an open hat on every off-beat
tips: Keep the kick soft so it is a pulse, not a punch.
The open hat sits on the off-beats.
Strings and a bright guitar give the strut.
howToBringIn: Kick and open hat first, then bass, then the strings.
beats.fast: Above 118 it is a house track.

beats.name: Slow afro groove
beats.say: boom . . boom | . . snap . | . boom . . | snap . . boom  (kicks fall in odd places, shaker keeps going)
tips: A constant shaker or hat carries the feel.
Give the kick a syncopated pattern, the snare as a rim click.
Fits sung melodies in a high register.
howToBringIn: Shaker and bass first, then the kick pattern.
beats.fast: Above 108 it turns into amapiano or afro house.

beats.name: Slow blues 12/8
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . SNAP . | . . . . | . . SNAP .  (in 4 slow, each beat a triplet)
tips: Play the hat or ride as triplets (swing 0.66).
The snare stays on 2 and 4 and is soft.
A slow, bending guitar line carries the melody.
howToBringIn: Guitar and bass first, the drums enter in the second verse.
beats.fast: Above 68 it is a mid-tempo shuffle.
beats.slow: Below 48 the triplets get too sluggish.

beats.name: Hypnotic techno
beats.say: BOOM . . . | BOOM . . . | BOOM . . . | BOOM . . .  with a short tick every off-beat and a ghost rim
tips: Change one detail every 8 bars (a tick, a filter).
Keep the kick steady, the interest lies in the percussion.
A short, dry stab loops as the melody.
howToBringIn: Kick alone for 8 bars, then hats, then a stab.

beats.name: Soft dembow
beats.say: BOOM . . snap | . BOOM snap . | BOOM . . snap | . BOOM snap .  (the classic dembow rock)
tips: Keep the snares tuned high and dry.
Leave space for a smooth vocal.
A muted synth or guitar plays chord stabs.
howToBringIn: Kick and snare first, add a synth bass after four bars.

beats.name: Deep house, warm
beats.say: BOOM . . . | BOOM . tss . | BOOM . . . | BOOM . tss .  (soft kick, off-beat open hat, a rim ghost)
tips: Keep the kick soft and round, the bass does the weight.
The chord stabs are short and jazzy.
howToBringIn: Kick and hat for 8 bars, then bass, then chords.

beats.name: Pop rock anthem
beats.say: BOOM . . . | SNARE . . boom | BOOM . . . | SNARE . . .  (kick on 1, snare on 2 and 4, 8th hats)
tips: Verse on hat, chorus on ride or open hat.
A snare roll leads into every chorus.
howToBringIn: Verse light, chorus with open hat and a crash on 1.
beats.fast: Above 130 it turns into driving rock.
beats.slow: Below 100 let the guitar arpeggio help.

beats.name: Pop-punk bounce
beats.say: BOOM . snare . | BOOM . snare . | all 8ths on the hat  (kick and snare trade every beat)
tips: The snare on every beat gives the bounce.
Short songs, tight stops at the end of lines.
howToBringIn: Everything from bar 1; the intro is a stop-and-go snare roll.
beats.slow: Below 150 it reads as pop rock.

beats.name: Post-punk tom drive
beats.say: tom . tom . | BOOM . tom SNARE | tom . tom . | BOOM . . SNARE  (toms lead, the hat barely plays)
tips: Let the toms carry the rhythm, not the hat.
A bass guitar riff repeats; the guitar answers in short stabs.
howToBringIn: Bass riff first, then toms, then kick and snare.

beats.name: Roots rockers
beats.say: BOOM . . . | snap . . . | BOOM . . . | snap . . .  (kick and snare together on 3, off-beat skank)
tips: The guitar skanks on the off-beat, short and dry.
Bass is round and melodic.
howToBringIn: Bass and drums first, the skank and organ join later.

beats.name: Dubstep half-time wobble
beats.say: BOOM . . . | . . . . | SNARE . . . | . . . .  (one kick on 1, one snare on 3, the bass does the rest)
tips: The wobble bass fills every gap.
Silence before the drop makes it hit.
howToBringIn: Intro with a pad, drop with the bass and the half-time kit.
beats.fast: Above 150 it is drum and bass.
beats.slow: Below 138 it is a heavy half-time beat.

beats.name: Liquid drum and bass roll
